title: Encryption and key custody
acceptance_scenarios: Inspect DB, filestore, audio, temporary/export copies, replicas and backups. Verify TLS, encrypted artifacts, legacy migration, separation of keys, rotation and controlled recovery.
evidence_after_implementation: A04-storage-coverage.csv; A04-TLS-report.pdf; redacted key/rotation records; migration results; encrypted-backup and recovery test report.
manual_acceptance: Infrastructure and security approve the estate/key inventory. A screenshot or encrypted field alone is insufficient. Refresh on storage, key, provider or encryption changes; schedule periodic checks.
history_policy: Do not invent legacy consent times, rewrite existing clinical seals, or record mock authority responses as real acceptance.
implemented_controls: Sensitive healthcare attachments use AES-256-GCM with transparent HTTP delivery and unchanged plaintext checksums. Scribe transcripts, correction reasons and AI coding payloads are encrypted; legacy plaintext columns are migrated without changing seals. Backup pairs use an external root-owned key.
remaining_actions: Production disk/database encryption, independent key escrow, custody and rotation must be arranged. Existing PHI derivation is preserved; database.secret remains available to an authorised DB administrator.
